pr_title: Allow configuring suppressApplicationTitle in new tab/pane/window commands
pr_body:
## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/9345
* [x] CLA signed. 
* [ ] Tests added/passed
* [x] Documentation updated - https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/terminal/pull/279
* [x] Schema updated.
* [ ] I've discussed this with core contributors already. 

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments
Introduce optional `suppressApplicationTitle` in to `NewTerminalArgs`.
When set (either to true or false) overrides profile configuration.

Introduce `--suppressApplicationTitle` flag to command line arguments.
When provided for sub=command, 
sets the value in the relevant `NewTerminalArgs` to `true`
pr_comments:
>

~The standard for CLI11 is `!--suppressApplicationTitle`, I can make it work I guess. WDYT?~
Ignore it.
I will add it :)

# Environment

```none
Windows build number: [run `[Environment]::OSVersion` for powershell, or `ver` for cmd]

Platform ServicePack Version      VersionString
-------- ----------- -------      -------------
 Win32NT             10.0.19042.0 Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19042.0
Windows Terminal version (if applicable): 1.7 Preview

Any other software?
```

# Steps to reproduce

1) Add a command to the settings.json file similar to this:

```
        {
            "command": 
            {
                "action": "newTab",
                "index": 1,
                "profile": "<whatever profile you want>",
                "startingDirectory": "<Whatever you want>",
                "tabTitle": "Test Title"
            },
            "keys": "ctrl+1"
        },
```

2) Save file.
3) In Terminal Window, press `ctrl+1` to create a new tab based on that command.


# Expected behavior

Expected (Ver 1.6): Tab title is "Test Title"

# Actual behavior

Actual: Tab title is the path the terminal window/tab is currently in.
comments: Perhaps the profile runs a program that changes the title. How is the profile defined?

If you want the tab title to persist, you'll have to add `"suppressApplicationTitle": true,` to the profile you're opening. Otherwise the tab title is being set by the command then reset by the shell.
If the `"splitPane"`, `"newTab"`, and `"newWindow"` actions support `"tabTitle"`, then perhaps they should support `"suppressApplicationTitle"` as well.

> If the `"splitPane"`, `"newTab"`, and `"newWindow"` actions support `"tabTitle"`, then perhaps they should support `"suppressApplicationTitle"` as well.

I actually don't hate that. Wouldn't be that hard to plumb through. I'm gonna re-open this just to track that idea. Thanks!


This shouldn't be too hard to add to the existing `NewTerminalArgs` class. 
* We'd need to parse a property like `"suppressApplicationTitle"` into an _optional_ bool (Probably needs to be a `Windows::Foundation::IReference<bool>`). When that key exists, then we'll override the profile's own `suppressApplicationTitle` property. When it's omitted, then we'll leave the setting alone.
* We should also add it as a commandline arg, to `AppCommandlineArgs`. Same deal - an optional flag.
On it. Actually this feature is must :smile:

review_comments: Should we add some kind of shorthand version of this? `suppressApplicationTitle` is one of the longest named settings we have, I think haha.
I am not sure, I usually write those once (in startupActions 😛 )
Yea, I say let's leave it for now, and if someone _really_ wants a single-character flag for it in the future, and has a good idea, then we can address it then.

This is totally off-topic to this PR, but something I wanted to discuss out loud. Since we get the profile and generate a `TerminalSettings` from it, that means we get base layer (or profiles.defaults) applied properly. Maybe we should emphasize this in the docs? I feel like most people that use this setting want to enable it on every profile, but that's just a gut feeling.

Actually I am not sure.. I usually use two types of tabs:
* General purpose ones, where I do change folders and stuff - I want the title to change
* Dedicated ones (e.g., git bash in terminal folder) that I don't  - I want the title to remain Terminal Dev.
